title: Passato Prossimo con Essere
subtitle: Motion and change-of-state verbs, and why the participle must agree.
objectives: Identify the common verbs that take essere as their auxiliary
Make the past participle agree with the subject when using essere
Recognize the essere pattern for reflexive verbs

content.intro: A smaller, learnable group of verbs — mostly about motion, staying, or a change of state — use essere instead of avere as their passato prossimo auxiliary, and this changes one important rule.
content.explanation: With essere, the past participle behaves like an adjective: it agrees in gender and number with the subject. The classic mnemonic for which verbs take essere is a short list learned by heart (often taught as "the house of essere"): andare, venire, partire, arrivare, entrare, uscire, salire, scendere, nascere, morire, diventare, stare, essere itself, rimanere, tornare, cadere, crescere.

rules.heading: a) Common essere verbs
rules.body:
• Motion: andare, venire, partire, arrivare, entrare, uscire, salire, scendere, tornare, cadere
  • Change of state: nascere (to be born), morire (to die), diventare (to become), crescere (to grow)
  • Staying: stare, rimanere

rules.heading: b) Participle agreement
rules.body: The participle takes -o (m. sing.), -a (f. sing.), -i (m. pl.), -e (f. pl.): Marco è andato. Maria è andata. I ragazzi sono andati. Le ragazze sono andate.

examples.it: I miei genitori sono partiti ieri.

examples.en: We got back late last night.
Have you ever been to Italy?

commonMistakes.why: Andare takes essere, not avere, as its auxiliary.
With essere, the participle must agree with the feminine subject Maria: andata, not andato.
Feminine plural subject needs the -e ending on the participle: arrivate.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Use the passato prossimo, making the participle agree with the subject.

items.explanation: Nascere takes essere, and the participle agrees with the feminine subject: nata.
Feminine plural subject needs the -e participle ending.
Nascere takes essere; masculine singular participle: nato.
Diventare takes essere; masculine singular participle: diventato.

items.prompt: Which verb takes essere in the passato prossimo?
items.explanation: Cadere (to fall) is one of the common essere verbs.

items.prompt: "Siamo rimasti a casa" — rimasti agrees with...
items.explanation: The -i ending marks a masculine plural subject.

items.statement: All motion verbs take essere in the passato prossimo.
items.explanation: It's a specific, learnable list of common verbs, not a blanket rule covering every verb of motion.

items.statement: Nascere and morire both take essere as their auxiliary.
items.explanation: Both are change-of-state verbs on the essere list.

summary: A learnable list of motion, change-of-state, and staying verbs take essere as their auxiliary.
With essere, the past participle agrees in gender and number with the subject.
With avere, the participle never agrees — this is the key contrast to remember.
